ops.body:
Design detail for daemon boot and shutdown. Source keeps terse contracts; this is the why. (Rewritten 2026-07-19 for the daemonkit migration — the old exact-equality eviction, evictPeer ladder, and wg-only drain are gone.)

## Startup goroutine ordering (startupTable)
One startup goroutine, off the accept path so Health answers from the first instant, runs the ordered startupTable strictly in order, then starts the loops. The ordering constraints:
- bridges bind BEFORE any mount/FP enumeration registers;
- holder.refresh primes the mount cache BEFORE selects key on it — mountReady's lazy refresh covers the residual bind→prime gap;
- ua.detect only stamps the OAuth User-Agent off the pre-bind path;
- overlays.reconcile finishes BEFORE the heal loop and scheduler, which both touch fuse Setup.

## listen() — single-entrant bind, takeover via daemonkit
Binds the unix socket (0600) under an exclusive flock on socket+".lock" (proc.SingleEntrant, held for the daemon's lifetime, NEVER removed — unlinking a held lock file would let a third daemon flock a fresh inode and reopen the race). The Evict closure is the only cc-pool policy: it runs daemonkit daemon.Run (RequestDaemon + SocketRelease, Grace = evictTimeout) behind the daemonPeer adapter — Health and the OpShutdown handshake over the daemon wire, with the victim pid read from the socket's SO_PEERCRED (kernel-attested, never a wire field), and takeover-only proto-TOLERANT reply decoding so a cross-proto incumbent takes the full ladder (public clients stay strict). Policy is newer-wins: a strictly-newer arrival evicts (Shutdown → grace → re-Health with pid/start-time revalidation → SIGKILL); same-or-newer incumbent → ExitSelf, exit 0, and the LaunchAgent's KeepAlive {SuccessfulExit=false} keeps the loser down. A downgrade no longer evicts (the old any-skew rule is gone; dev sentinels still beat releases). A flock held without a bound socket resolves by poll-then-ErrLockStillHeld, not ErrPeerStarting.

## handle() — lifecycle ops before the proto gate
OpHealth and OpShutdown dispatch BEFORE the proto-version gate (they are the takeover probe — a cross-proto successor must read the incumbent's version) and stay OFF drain admission but ON the serve waitgroup, so a shutdown ACK always lands before the process exits. Work ops sit behind the proto gate and drain admission.

## serve() — settle-before-cancel drain
Shutdown runs drain.Simple: close both listeners (daemon + sync RPC), settle admitted work — sync handlers included — then cancel executors (whose ctx is context.WithoutCancel of the signal ctx precisely so settlement outlives the signal), then wait the background loops. In-flight requests complete to terminal responses; new work is refused at admission. The store closes only after everything above.
